title: Acme Health - SOC2 / ISO 27001 posture review
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate link (Trust Center)
Redwood SE to send controls-mapping spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to Acme Health requirements
Schedule a follow-up demo of audit-logs and retention controls (30-45 minutes)
Provide SAML/SSO integration guide and sample SAML metadata for Okta
Confirm data residency options and VPC/on-prem checklist for Acme Health pilot
action_items: Priya Desai (Redwood) - Share SOC 2 Type II report PDF and ISO 27001 cert link via secure share - due 2025-03-24
Jordan Lee (Redwood) - Send controls mapping spreadsheet and Trust Center link - due 2025-03-21
Maria Gonzalez (Acme) - Share Acme's compliance checklist and specific control gaps - due 2025-03-28
Priya Desai (Redwood) - Schedule audit log demo and invite Acme security + infra - due 2025-03-26
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're scheduled for 45 minutes. quick intros?
[00:05] Maria Gonzalez: Hi Maria here, head of infosec at Acme. we want to run through your SOC2 and ISO posture and how we can map controls, we've got some regulators asking for evidence soon.
[00:15] Ethan Park: Ethan, CTO. we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated for PHI workflows, latency also matters but sec/compliance is blocker right now.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Great, Jordan AE here, and Priya is our SE who will cover the technical controls and audit logs. Priya over to you?
[00:35] Priya Desai: thanks. quick agenda: trust center artifacts, controls mapping, SSO/RBAC, encryption/KMS, audit logs & retention, and deployment options (VPC/dedicated). sound good?
[01:05] Lena Kim: yes that works. timeline constraints: compliance team needs evidence for SOC2 Type II and ISO mapping within 2 weeks if possible.

[01:25] Priya Desai: understood. first the artifacts: we maintain a Trust Center with links to our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. I'll share the secure link after the call — it's behind an authenticated page. it's similar to: https://trust.redwood.ai (note: placeholder).
[02:10] Maria Gonzalez: how recent is the SOC2? and is it full Type II with monitoring period?

[02:20] Priya Desai: yes Type II, latest audit period ended 2024-11. it covers our hosted and dedicated control scope; report includes tests of operating effectiveness. we'll provide redacted report on the Trust Center link.
[03:00] Ethan Park: for ISO 27001 do you have the full cert and scope? does it include the private deployment option?

[03:12] Priya Desai: we have ISO 27001 cert and statement of applicability. scope covers control plane and customer workload hosting in our supported regions. for private/on-prem we provide a separate controls checklist — we'll include that in the controls mapping spreadsheet.

[04:00] Maria Gonzalez: key for us is evidence mapping to our control set: access control, encryption at rest/in transit, key management, audit logging, vulnerability mgmt, vendor mgmt. can you map Redwood controls to those?
[04:18] Jordan Lee: absolutely, we'll send a controls-mapping XLSX that maps Redwood SOC2/ISO controls to customer control IDs and suggested evidence artifacts.

[04:40] Priya Desai: on auth and access: we support SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Azure AD), SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC at the org/team/route level. you can grant roles and restrict model access. some customers tie it to their IdP for automated deprovisioning.
[05:25] Lena Kim: does SCIM sync group membership and remove tokens on deprovision? we need proof for offboarding controls.
[05:40] Priya Desai: yes SCIM can sync and we have a token revocation API. we'll attach the SAML/SCIM integration guide; it has sample metadata and how we handle session TTLs and token rotation.
[06:20] Maria Gonzalez: audit logs — we need immutable logs with export capability and retention controls. what granularity and retention options do you offer?

[06:35] Priya Desai: we emit request-level audit logs with user, org, route, model, timestamp, token cost, and request/response metadata (response bodies redacted by default). logs are stored in our audit pipeline and we offer configurable retention for Dedicated/Private. hosted customers can request extended retention as an add-on. we'll demo the log viewer and export during follow-up.
[07:10] Ethan Park: are logs tamper-evident / do you support append-only or integration with our SIEM?

[07:20] Priya Desai: logs are write-once in our internal pipeline and we support streaming to customer SIEMs via secure forwarders (S3, Kinesis, or syslog endpoints). for tamper-evidence you can enable log shipping to your own immutable bucket and retain object-lock if required.
[08:05] Maria Gonzalez: encryption and KMS — do you manage keys or can we bring our own (BYOK)?

[08:18] Priya Desai: both. by default data at rest is encrypted with provider-managed keys; for Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, Cloud KMS, or customer HSM). we also support envelope encryption; KMS operations are logged.
[09:00] Lena Kim: does BYOK cover model cache/KV cache and persisted artifacts? we need assurance that cached tokens or prefix caches are encrypted.
[09:12] Priya Desai: yes KV cache and disk attachments are encrypted with the same KMS keys in the environment. in Dedicated you can pin the key policy and rotate as needed.
[09:50] Jordan Lee: note: sometimes our internal transcript auto transcribes "KV cache" as "K V cache", so docs will show the correct term. just flagging for audit reviewers.
[10:10] Maria Gonzalez: data residency — can we restrict all processing to a specific region like us-east-1? PHI flows require US-only processing and logs staying in US.

[10:25] Priya Desai: yes we offer region pinning for deployments and data residency controls. Dedicated or Private deployments give you full control. hosted customers can request region pinning for the active model region; we'll confirm the exact region endpoints available for your account.
[11:05] Ethan Park: about dedicated vs hosted: cost vs compliance tradeoff. if we go hosted but need strict evidence, is that supported?

[11:20] Priya Desai: hosted can meet many controls via our Trust Center and artifact sharing; for the strictest isolation and BYOK, Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private are better. we can run a short pilot in Dedicated to validate controls with your auditors.
[12:00] Maria Gonzalez: can you show the access logs that tie an action to a user and the API key or SSO identity?
[12:12] Priya Desai: yes logs include user identity, session id, route, model, and api key hashes. we'll prepare a sanitized sample log export for your review.
[13:00] Lena Kim: vulnerability management — how often do you run scans and do you share pen-test results?

[13:12] Priya Desai: we do quarterly vulnerability scans, regular internal pentests and annual external pentests; summary results and remediation status can be shared under NDA. the SOC2 report also covers vulnerability mgmt procedures.
[14:00] Jordan Lee: question from Acme earlier about change management and code deployment audits — covered in SOC2?
[14:12] Priya Desai: yes change management and code review controls are included in our SOC2 scope. we'll call out specific sections in the mapping doc.
[15:00] Maria Gonzalez: regarding logging retention durations: what's default and what tiers allow extended retention?

[15:12] Priya Desai: default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs, with options up to 365 days as add-on. Dedicated/Private allow arbitrary retention since you manage the destination (S3 with lifecycle or your SIEM).
[16:00] Ethan Park: do you support field-level redaction or PII scrubbing in logs?
[16:12] Priya Desai: yes redaction rules can be applied server-side and for Dedicated we can customize the scrubbing pipeline. we redact model outputs by default in hosted unless configured.
[17:00] Maria Gonzalez: auditors also want evidence of least privilege for service accounts — can you provide token usage reports?
[17:12] Priya Desai: we provide token usage reports and token rotation logs; SCIM provisioning events are logged too. we'll include an example report in the artifacts package.

[18:00] Jordan Lee: quick note on compliance gating — typical next step is we share Trust Center artifacts and a controls map, you review and identify gaps, then we schedule a deeper audit-log demo and test pilot if needed.
[18:20] Maria Gonzalez: sounds good. please ensure the controls mapping highlights any residual risks that would require Dedicated/private deployment.
[19:00] Priya Desai: will do. also we can provide a short checklist for auditors: list of artifacts and where to find them, contact for further evidence requests.
[20:00] Ethan Park: timing — Maria wants this done within two weeks. is that feasible?
[20:12] Jordan Lee: yes we'll prioritize the artifact share this week; action items reflected. we'll aim to have the Trust Center links and mapping by Friday.
[21:00] Maria Gonzalez: one more question — do you support customer-managed keys for TLS or only at rest?
[21:12] Priya Desai: we manage TLS certs for endpoints but for Private deployments you can front with your own TLS termination. mutual TLS support is available for private endpoints.
[22:00] Lena Kim: any network segmentation docs? we need specifics on VPC peering, private endpoints, and routing rules.
[22:12] Priya Desai: yes we have a VPC/on-prem checklist and network diagram pack; will include that in the attachment bundle.
[23:00] Jordan Lee: ok let's recap action items and follow-ups
[23:10] Maria Gonzalez: recap appreciated

[23:20] Jordan Lee: recap: Redwood sends SOC2/ISO artifacts via Trust Center link, SE sends controls mapping, SAML/SCIM guide, and sample audit logs. schedule audit-log demo — we'll propose times next week. Acme to share compliance checklist. any other items?
[23:45] Maria Gonzalez: that's it from our side, thanks. we'll review and come back with gap list.
[24:00] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone — end call.
